### UTC Date & Time

[October 23, 2025, 14:00 UTC](https://savvytime.com/converter/utc/oct-23-2025/2pm)

### Agenda

- Fusaka
  - testnet updates by @barnabasbusa
    - Sepolia BPO1 recap
    - upcoming: Sepolia BPO2, Hoodi
  - [mainnet dates confirmation request](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1764#issuecomment-3412633683) by @ralexstokes
    - [document with candidate dates](https://notes.ethereum.org/@bbusa/fusaka-bpo-timeline)
    - [alternative BPO timing](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1764#issuecomment-3435616551)
    - [comment](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1764#issuecomment-3413398303) by @abcoathup: wait with official date setting until after testnets
- Glamsterdam
  - devnet updates?
  - [non-headliner EIP process proposal](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1764#issuecomment-3433396802) by @ralexstokes and @adietrichs
  - [repricing topics](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1764#issuecomment-3436247707) by @misilva73
    - temperature check: best approach for increased gas precision
    - proposal for breakout calls
  - EIPs to potentially remove from PFI:
    - [EIP-7667 because of lack of champion](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1764#issuecomment-3423909327)
    - [EIP-6873 because of Verkle dependency](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1764#issuecomment-3435358557)
  - [EIP-8058 presentation](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1764#issuecomment-3436742283) by @CPerezz
  - open discussion

comments.body:
i'd like to go ahead and confirm Fusaka mainnet (again, assuming the rest of our testnets go well) following the mainnet dates here from @barnabasbusa https://notes.ethereum.org/@bbusa/fusaka-bpo-timeline

we covered the topic on ACDC#167 and there was no issue with 3 Nov mainnet releases for a 3 Dec mainnet date

note: BPO1 and BPO2 are also scheduled in the doc

>confirm Fusaka mainnet (again, assuming the rest of our testnets go well) 

@ralexstokes assume we shouldn't confirm (set) the proposed date until after Hoodi testnet upgrades

> Mainnet should not have an upgrade date set until all testnets have been upgraded.

*From: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/processes/protocol-upgrade.md#mainnet*

@abcoathup right, so i'd like to get a soft-confirmation on this week's call

this is so core devs have a 3 Nov date on their schedule for mainnet releases

we can wait until ACDC on 30 Oct to make the dates official

in either world, we would obviously hold off if the hoodi fork doesn't go well

[EIP7667](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7667): 
- It was added to Glamsterdam's PFIs [when the meta EIP was created](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commits/master/EIPS/eip-7773.md) as a hold over from "the verkle fork"
- It was originally proposed by Vitalik in [an April 2024 ACDE call](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/AllCoreDevs-EL-Meetings/Meeting%20185.md)
- It doesn't currently have a ["champion"](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10391)
- Its sole author is Vitalik, who can't be added as a reasonable default "point of contact" for obvious reasons
- If no one is willing to champion it, I think it should be removed from PFI

p.s. all PFI'd EIP champions are now [displayed on Forkcast](https://forkcast.org/upgrade/glamsterdam#proposed-for-inclusion)

was discussing with ansgar and we'd like to make the process suggested around handling Glamsterdam non-headliners a bit more concrete as we move from Fusaka into Glamsterdam scoping

1. seems like we can start as of this call with thinking about glamsterdam non-headliner selection
2. i'd propose we use this call as the time to flag that there is **1 more week** to propose EIPs as non-headliners with deadline 30 Oct (next ACDC)
3. given the large number of EL EIPs to scope, i think getting written client opinions would be useful -- this can be as high-level (general themes) or as fine-grained (concrete list of EIPs) as a client team would like to chime in on, but having these opinions **before 6 Nov** would set ACDE up to finish Glamsterdam scoping by **end of November** (assuming it takes a few calls from there to get to rough consensus on the final set)

there's a smaller scoping task on the CL side and expect no issues there getting to a final Glam scope by end of november

let's use this as a starting point and can discuss on this call if we need to adjust anything

> [EIP7667](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7667):

> * If no one is willing to champion it, I think it should be removed from PFI

@nixorokish I think in principle there are still people that think pricing precompiles for zk cost would be preferable. I agree that the lack of champion is not ideal though. I remember @Sophia-Gold arguing for similar changes in the past, maybe she would be a candidate for EIP champion?

Separately, I saw that with [EIP-6873](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6873) we have another Verkle related EIP still in the list. That one looks to me like there would be no reason for inclusion without Verkle, so this could be another candidate for removal.

There was a bit of pushback on the BPO1 schedule from some teams, saying that if something goes wrong we gonna have a lot of people off on holidays already so late in december. Therefore an alternative BPO schedule is going to be proposed below:

| Network | Fork Name | Time UTC            | Epoch   | Start Slot  | Unix Timestamp | Notes
| ------- | --------- | ------------------:| -------:| -----------:| -------------:|---:|
Mainnet |	Fusaka |	2025-12-03 21:49:11	|411392|	13,164,544|	1764798551|	Same as before
Mainnet|	BPO 1	|2025-12-09 14:21:11	|412672|	13,205,504|	1765290071|	**Modified**
Mainnet|	BPO 2	|2026-01-07 01:01:11	|419072|	13,410,304|	1767747671|	Same as before

> > confirm Fusaka mainnet (again, assuming the rest of our testnets go well)
> 
> [@ralexstokes](https://github.com/ralexstokes) assume we shouldn't confirm (set) the proposed date until after Hoodi testnet upgrades
> 
> > Mainnet should not have an upgrade date set until all testnets have been upgraded.
> 
> _From: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/processes/protocol-upgrade.md#mainnet_

Here is my suggestion to change that: 

https://github.com/ethereum/pm/pull/1780

For more context on the the breakout call, the proposal is to have two breakout calls to discuss the repricing EIPs that are PFI in Glamsterdam. The proposed times are:
 - Call 1: Wednesday, Oct 29th, 15:00 UTC
 - Call 2: Wednesday, Nov 5th, 15:00 UTC
The goal is to do a deep dive on each repricing EIP, discuss potential issues and gather some consensus on prioritization. At the end, we wil report back on the key takeaways in the following ACDE.

I wanted to add to the agenda the proposal and a short/minimal presentation on [EIP-8058 - Contract Bytecode deduplication discount](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8058-contract-bytecode-deduplication-discount/25933)

The zkEVM team discussed [EIP7667](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7667) and don't think it's a good idea for Glamsterdam because we won't be able to use numbers from real benchmarks by then. We told this to Maria so hopefully it's been removed from the Meta EIP by now.

In the future, can we not automatically propose old EIPs and instead require a person to propose each one for a specific hard fork?
[EIP7667](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7667) is not yet removed from the Repricings Meta EIP, @Sophia-Gold , but I will do it tomorrow

> Separately, I saw that with [EIP-6873](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6873) we have another Verkle related EIP still in the list. That one looks to me like there would be no reason for inclusion without Verkle, so this could be another candidate for removal.

I'm strictly proposing 7667 for removal because of its lack of champion - Guillaume is the champion for 6873 so it's not relevant in this vein
Here are the [slides](https://notes.ethereum.org/@misilva/Hy6o1OLRgx#/) from the rounding error discussion.

> short/minimal presentation on EIP-8058

@CPerezz can you please share your slides?

> > short/minimal presentation on EIP-8058
> 
> [@CPerezz](https://github.com/CPerezz) can you please share your slides?

https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1FMA3ndWBfTdvtqQlg4l2thy4E6rnSvwnz0G6cjkwN9I/edit?usp=sharing

There you go!
